slide_01_tambopata_net.title: Net new mining in the Tambopata buffer zone fell 90% in 2019–21, then came back
slide_01_tambopata_net.subtitle: Net annual addition to mapped mining area (this year minus last year), ha per year. Shaded: 2019–21.
slide_01_tambopata_net.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru, Collection 4 (class 4.2 Minería), course table peru_bufferzone_year.csv (all department rows summed). Net additions can hide returns to old pits. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_02a_zones.title: La Pampa: land mined for the first time halved in 2019–21
slide_02a_zones.subtitle: Land mined for the first time, ha per year (a new measure: not net additions). La Pampa sector: 1,395 → 722 → 987 ha/yr (2016–18 → 2019–21 → 2022–25).
slide_02a_zones.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), cut to our zones (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; legal corridor = D.L. 1100, INGEMMET). First-time mining = pixels mapped as mining for the first time since 1985. Legality is by location; the map class can't tell legal from illegal mining. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_02b_zones.title: Madre de Dios as a whole didn't fall: new mining grew in the legal corridor
slide_02b_zones.subtitle: Land mined for the first time, ha per year. All Madre de Dios: 5,317 → 6,571 → 11,373 ha/yr; legal corridor share 49% → 68% → 72% (mean of yearly shares).
slide_02b_zones.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), cut to our zones (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; legal corridor = D.L. 1100, INGEMMET). First-time mining = pixels mapped as mining for the first time since 1985. Legality is by location; the map class can't tell legal from illegal mining. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_03_road_share.title: New mining near La Pampa moved north of the highway: 23% → 65% of first-time mining
slide_03_road_share.subtitle: Share of land mined for the first time that lies north of the Interoceanic Highway, within La Pampa's longitudes (±30 km). The road had been crossed before: most new mining was north of it in 2008–10.
slide_03_road_share.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), cut to our zones (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; legal corridor = D.L. 1100, INGEMMET). First-time mining = pixels mapped as mining for the first time since 1985. North = legal corridor side; south = Tambopata buffer zone. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_03b_road_bands.title: In 2019–21 new mining near La Pampa piled up just north of the road
slide_03b_road_bands.subtitle: Land mined for the first time per year, by 1-km band from the Interoceanic Highway within La Pampa's longitudes. North share 23% → 65%.
slide_03b_road_bands.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), cut to our zones (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; legal corridor = D.L. 1100, INGEMMET). First-time mining = pixels mapped as mining for the first time since 1985. Bands shown to ±15 km; shares use all bands to ±30 km. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_04_context.title: Enforcement money peaked in 2019 and faded, while gold rose 2.7-fold (2018–25)
slide_04_context.subtitle: Same years in each panel. Solid line: Mercurio (Feb 2019); shaded: 2019–21; dashed: COVID, Restauración, emergency, navy out. Spending is a lower bound.
slide_04_context.source: Source: MEF Consulta Amigable, PP 0128 executed spending (devengado), Madre de Dios; World Bank Pink Sheet (nominal); MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), cut to our zones (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; legal corridor = D.L. 1100, INGEMMET). First-time mining = pixels mapped as mining for the first time since 1985. Correlation is not shown: 11 years, and money follows mining.

slide_05_old_pits.title: In 2023, 67% of new mining in La Pampa was on old pits
slide_05_old_pits.subtitle: La Pampa sector, ha per year: land mined for the first time vs land mined before (not last year) and mined again. Forest-loss alerts and net additions miss most of this.
slide_05_old_pits.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4 annual maps (30 m, class 4.2 mining, legal and illegal), cut to our zones (La Pampa sector = Tambopata buffer zone 70.15–69.80° W; legal corridor = D.L. 1100, INGEMMET). First-time mining = pixels mapped as mining for the first time since 1985. Old-pit counts include some year-to-year map flicker (252 ha/yr already in 2016–18): trust the 2023 jump, not small changes. MAAP #193 (2023) reports miners back on degraded land. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_06_reserve.title: In 2025, mining inside Tambopata National Reserve jumped by 241 ha
slide_06_reserve.subtitle: Net annual addition to mapped mining area inside the reserve itself (not the buffer zone), ha. Total inside in 2025: 777 ha. The 2025 jump follows the navy's withdrawal from the Malinowski River posts (MAAP #241, 2026).
slide_06_reserve.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4, protected-area statistics (class 4.2 Minería; platform check 777 ha, 2025). MAAP #241 (Pacsi et al., 2026) reports ~500 ha inside the reserve, late 2025 to Feb 2026. Satellites cannot see river dredges or mercury.

slide_07_causal.title: In hectares, Tambopata's 2019–21 fall is the largest of 15 Peruvian buffer zones
slide_07_causal.subtitle: Each dot: one buffer zone's 2019–21 change after zone and year effects. Left = bigger fall.
slide_07_causal.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4, peru_bufferzone_year.csv; 15 Peruvian buffer zones with mining before 2019 (scaled: 7 with > 10 ha/yr). Tambopata removed from each fake zone's comparison pool. Placebo p = rank / n.

slide_07b_estimates.title: The estimates range from about 400 to 1,900 ha a year less net new mining
slide_07b_estimates.subtitle: Causal only if the other Peruvian buffer zones show what Tambopata would otherwise have done. In hectares only; coincides with COVID.
slide_07b_estimates.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Collection 4, peru_bufferzone_year.csv; zone + year effects (M1–M3), synthetic control and synthetic DiD on the same 15-zone panel (peru_models.py, peru_sdid.py).

slide_08_brazil_twins.title: Tambopata grew faster than its Brazilian twins before 2019, so they can't show the counterfactual
slide_08_brazil_twins.subtitle: Left: parallel pre-trends are rejected for both twins (p < 0.001). Right: in 2019–21 Tambopata grew more slowly than both. A second check only, never the main comparison. Brazil 2019–22 also had weak federal enforcement.
slide_08_brazil_twins.source: Source: MapBiomas Peru Col 4 (Tambopata) and MapBiomas Amazonía Col 6 (twins) before 2019; Amazon Mining Watch (480 m) for 2019–21. Different collections: compared as indices, never subtracted. Twins chosen by fixed rules (control_select.py).
